title: Summer Intern 2027 – Quantitative Researcher (PhD) at Five Rings in New York | $300,000 Salary, Sign-On Bonus & Corporate Housing
summary: If you are a PhD student with exceptional quantitative and programming skills, the Five Rings Summer Intern 2027 – Quantitative Researcher (PhD) program offers an outstanding opportunity to gain hands-on experience at one of the world s leading proprietary trading firms. Based in New York , this highly competitive 9-week paid internship combines cutting-edge quantitative research, real-world trading strategy development, mentorship, technical training, and professional networking. With an annualized base salary of $300,000 , plus a sign-on bonus and corporate housing , this internship is designed for talented doctoral students who are passionate about solving complex mathematical problems and applying quantitative research to financial markets. Whether your background is in computer science, mathematics, statistics, economics, physics, or another quantitative discipline, this internship provides a unique opportunity to work alongside world-class researchers and traders while gaining practical experience in quantitative finance. About Five Rings Five Rings is a proprietary trading firm that combines technology, quantitative research, innovation, and strategic thinking to compete successfully in global financial markets. Founded with the goal of building sophisticated trading strategies through advanced research and technology, the firm operates offices in: New York Boca Raton London Amsterdam The company trades across numerous domestic and international markets, continually identifying new opportunities, evaluating risks, and developing innovative strategies. One of Five Rings defining characteristics is its collaborative culture. Employees are encouraged to exchange ideas freely across teams, creating an environment where innovation and continuous learning thrive. About the Summer Internship Program The Five Rings Quantitative Research Internship is a full-time, intensive 9-week summer program designed specifically for PhD students pursuing careers in quantitative research and algorithmic trading. The internship runs: From the beginning of June Through the beginning of August During the program, interns become integrated members of the research team and contribute directly to projects that influence real trading strategies. Rather than simply observing professionals, interns actively participate in solving real research challenges. What Interns Will Do Throughout the internship, successful candidates will: Work on real quantitative research projects Develop mathematical models Analyze financial market data Collaborate with experienced quantitative researchers Build research tools Improve existing trading strategies Explore innovative quantitative techniques Solve challenging mathematical problems Present ideas and findings Interns work closely with experienced professionals who provide guidance throughout the program. Dedicated Mentorship One of the strongest features of the internship is its mentorship structure. Every intern is paired with a mentor who is fully dedicated to supporting their learning and development throughout the internship. Mentors help interns: Navigate research projects Improve technical skills Understand trading concepts Develop quantitative thinking Receive continuous feedback Grow professionally This personalized mentorship allows interns to maximize their learning experience over the nine-week program. Training and Learning Opportunities Beyond project work, interns participate in structured educational sessions covering essential trading and quantitative finance concepts. The program includes: Classroom instruction Technical lectures Trading concept seminars Strategy development workshops In-house strategy games Practical research exercises These sessions are designed to provide a strong foundation in proprietary trading while helping interns understand how quantitative research supports financial decision-making. Collaborative and Social Experience Five Rings believes that strong collaboration leads to stronger innovation. Throughout the internship, participants enjoy numerous networking and team-building activities, including: Strategy game nights Team dinners Social events across New York Networking opportunities Informal discussions with experienced researchers and traders These activities help interns build professional relationships while experiencing the firm s collaborative culture. Who Should Apply? Five Rings is seeking highly talented PhD students who possess exceptional analytical ability and strong quantitative skills. Ideal candidates should: Be currently pursuing a PhD Demonstrate outstanding mathematical ability Enjoy solving highly complex problems Think creatively Learn quickly Work well both independently and collaboratively Be detail-oriented Be proactive Have strong curiosity Enjoy challenging research environments Eligible Fields of Study Applicants should be pursuing a PhD in one of the following or a related quantitative discipline: Computer Science Mathematics Physics Statistics Economics Other qualifying quantitative fields Candidates from related disciplines with strong mathematical and computational backgrounds are also encouraged to apply. Programming Skills Applicants should possess basic programming experience obtained through: Academic research Previous internships University coursework Research projects Programming skills are essential since quantitative research relies heavily on computational modeling and data analysis. Desired Qualities Five Rings is looking for candidates who demonstrate: Exceptional quantitative reasoning Strong mathematical intuition Analytical thinking Intellectual curiosity Independent problem solving Team collaboration Initiative Precision Attention to detail Passion for learning Internship Benefits Selected interns receive a highly competitive compensation package that includes: Annualized base salary of $300,000 Sign-on bonus Corporate housing Dedicated mentorship Hands-on research experience Professional training Exposure to proprietary trading strategies Networking opportunities Social and team-building events Classroom instruction Real-world quantitative research projects Why This Internship Stands Out The Five Rings Quantitative Research Internship is much more than a traditional internship. Participants receive: Direct exposure to quantitative finance Practical experience with real research challenges One-on-one mentorship Collaborative learning environment Industry-leading compensation Opportunities to develop advanced research skills Access to experienced researchers and traders The combination of technical learning, mentorship, and real-world application makes this one of the most prestigious internships available to PhD students interested in quantitative finance. Salary and Compensation Interns receive an impressive compensation package that includes: Annual Base Salary: $300,000 Sign-on bonus Corporate housing during the internship This reflects Five Rings commitment to attracting outstanding quantitative talent from around the world. Application Information Interested candidates should prepare a strong application highlighting: Academic achievements Quantitative skills Mathematical background Programming experience Research accomplishments Problem-solving abilities Candidates with demonstrated excellence in research and quantitative analysis are encouraged to apply. Click HERE to read more and apply. Conclusion The Five Rings Summer Intern 2027 – Quantitative Researcher (PhD) internship is an exceptional opportunity for doctoral students who aspire to work at the intersection of mathematics, technology, and financial markets. Through challenging research projects, dedicated mentorship, technical training, and exposure to proprietary trading strategies, interns gain invaluable experience while working alongside leading quantitative researchers. Combined with a generous compensation package—including a $300,000 annualized salary , sign-on bonus, and corporate housing—this internship represents one of the most competitive and rewarding research opportunities available for PhD students in quantitative disciplines. If you have a passion for mathematics, programming, and solving complex problems, this internship provides an excellent platform to advance your career in quantitative finance. title: Fully Funded AfriMAB GRÓ-LRT Land Restoration Fellowships 2027 in Iceland – Applications Open
summary: Applications are now open for the AfriMAB GRÓ-LRT Land Restoration Fellowships 2027 , a fully funded six-month training opportunity in Iceland for professionals working in African biosphere reserves and engaged in ecosystem restoration, sustainable land management, and related fields. The fellowship is jointly offered by AfriMAB , the network of UNESCO biosphere reserves in Africa, and Iceland’s GRÓ Land Restoration Training Programme (GRÓ LRT) . Selected fellows will undertake postgraduate-level training at the Agricultural University of Iceland , combining academic coursework, practical training, field visits, and an individual land restoration project. The 2027 programme begins on 26 February 2027 , and applications must be submitted by 10 September 2026 . AfriMAB GRÓ-LRT Land Restoration Fellowships 2027: Key Details Host Country: Iceland Host Institution: Agricultural University of Iceland Programme: GRÓ Land Restoration Training Programme (GRÓ LRT) Duration: Six months Start Date: 26 February 2027 Funding: Fully funded Target Group: Professionals working with African biosphere reserves Age Requirement: Under 40 years Academic Award: 30 ECTS postgraduate credits and GRÓ LRT Diploma Application Deadline: 10 September 2026 Applications open for AfriMAB GRÓ-LRT Land Restoration Fellowships 2027 Applications are now open for the 2027 AfriMAB GRÓ LRT Land Restoration Fellowships, offering fully funded places for professionals from African biosphere reserves engaged in ecosystem restoration. GRÓ LRT/UNESCO 17 July 2026 Last update:23 July 2026 Summary A six-month, hands-on programme Conditions and criteria More information AfriMAB, the network of UNESCO biosphere reserves across Africa, and Iceland s GRÓ Land Restoration Training Programme (GRÓ LRT) have opened applications for the 2027 cohort of their joint fellowship for professionals from African biosphere reserves. Selected candidates will spend six months, from 26 February 2027, at the Agricultural University of Iceland, combining coursework with an individual restoration project tailored to their home institution s needs, before returning to their posts with a postgraduate diploma and university credits. The fellowship which covers tuition, travel, health insurance, and a full living stipend responds to the growing priority restoration has taken on within the MAB Programme s agenda, responding to calls issued by the 2023 AfriMAB General Assembly and the UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration. Candidates under the age of 40 with relevant academic and field experience have until 10 September 2026 to submit their applications. GRÓ LRT/UNESCO Over the past four months in the GRÓ LRT program, I have gained valuable experience in restoration through theoretical and practical sessions, all the while building meaningful networks with fellows, alumni, and staff. Beyond technical knowledge, living in Iceland, the “land of fire and ice,” has broadened my perspective and deepened my appreciation of nature. This journey has inspired me professionally and personally. Neba Estherbel Bih, Cameroon, GRÓ LRT 2026 cohort A six-month, hands-on programme In 2019, the GRÓ Category 2 Centre was established to work across four thematic areas: Gender, fisheries, geothermal, and land restoration. The GRÓ Land Restoration Training Programme (GRÓ LRT) provides postgraduate training for working specialists from middle- and low-income countries in the restoration of degraded land and sustainable land management. The GRÓ LRT programme runs an annual six-month training in Iceland, hosted at the Agricultural University of Iceland. The first 12 weeks focus on coursework — introductory and specialized — alongside practical training and field trips. In the following 12 weeks, each Fellow develops an individual project tailored to their academic background and the needs of their home institution. Fellows who complete the training receive 30 ECTS at postgraduate level from the Agricultural University of Iceland, as well as a GRÓ LRT diploma. In this context, GRÓ LRT offers to train at least two fellows from African biosphere reserves engaged in restoration activities in its 2027 cohort. Applications are open The deadline is 10 September 2026 . Check conditions below. Conditions and criteria The fellowship is fully funded, covering tuition and academic expenses, travel and health insurance costs, and a stipend covering all living expenses during the six-month stay in Iceland. Institutions nominating a candidate are asked to grant them full study leave for the six-month training in Iceland, continue paying their salary and benefits throughout the programme, and reinstate them in their position upon their return. Applicants should hold a prominent role in ecosystem restoration activity within a biosphere reserve, and hold at least one university degree relevant to GRÓ LRT s field of work, such as ecology, natural sciences, environmental management or studies, and related disciplines. Candidates must: have at least one year of relevant experience working in a biosphere reserve; be able to communicate in English (speak, read and write), the working language of GRÓ LRT; be under the age of 40. In some cases, GRÓ LRT has accepted candidates who do not fulfil the education requirement but bring extensive working experience in a relevant area. Applicants must submit: a letter of motivation; a CV; a letter of endorsement from the biosphere reserve where they work; a letter of endorsement from the national MAB Focal Point or MAB Committee in their country, and; certificates of academic achievement. All documents must be uploaded in PDF form as attachments via the online application form. Applications are evaluated jointly by GRÓ LRT and the MAB Secretariat, and only complete applications meeting the stated requirements will be considered. The deadline for applications is 10 September 2026. For further information, contact grolrt@grolrt.is or mab@unesco.org . More information GRÓ Category 2 Centre UNESCO s Man and the Biosphere Programme Source: https://www.unesco.org/en/articles/applications-open-afrimab-gro-lrt-land-restoration-fellowships-2027 The post Fully Funded AfriMAB GRÓ-LRT Land Restoration Fellowships 2027 in Iceland – Applications Open appeared first on Opportunities for Youth .

title: UNESCO/Japan Young Researchers’ Fellowships Programme 2026: Up to US$10,000 for Research in Japan
summary: Applications are now open for the UNESCO/Japan Young Researchers’ Fellowships Programme 2026 , also known as the UNESCO/Keizo Obuchi Research Fellowships Programme . The programme offers young researchers from eligible countries the opportunity to undertake postgraduate research at universities and research institutions in Japan , with fellowship funding of up to US$10,000 . For the 2026 cycle, 10 fellowships will be awarded to highly qualified young researchers, with priority given to applicants from Africa, Small Island Developing States (SIDS), Ukraine and Türkiye . Research stays will focus on areas including heritage conservation, sustainable development, artificial intelligence, climate action, education and societal resilience . Application Deadline: 30 September 2026, midnight Paris time Fellowship Amount: Up to US$10,000 Number of Fellowships: 10 Host Country: Japan Duration: 3–9 months Research Period: From February 2027, to be completed by December 2027 Age Limit: 40 years or younger at the time of application Minimum Qualification: Master’s degree or equivalent Application Route: Through the applicant’s National Commission for UNESCO Notice: The application for the Cycle 2026 is now open. Deadline for Candidate Submission: 30 September 2026 Useful documents for the Cycle 2026 Application Guide Annex 1 – List of invited Member States and Associate Members Annex 2 – Research areas and indicative sub-areas Annex 3 – Application Form Annex 4 – Research Proposal Template Annex 5 – UNESCO Certificate of Language Knowledge About the Programme Established in 2001 under the Japanese Funds-in-Trust for the Capacity-Building of Human Resources, the UNESCO/Japan Young Researchers’ Fellowships Programme, also known as the UNESCO/Keizo Obuchi Research Fellowships Programme, is a long-standing initiative supported by the Government of Japan to strengthen research capacities and promote international knowledge exchange in areas aligned with UNESCO’s mandate. Since its establishment, the Programme has enabled 291 young researchers from 101 countries around the world to pursue postgraduate research, contributing to academic cooperation, capacity-building and the development of knowledge in fields of shared global importance. Under the 2026 cycle, UNESCO and the Government of Japan will award 10 fellowships to highly qualified young researchers from Africa, Small Island Developing States, Ukraine and Türkiye. The fellowships will support innovative and high-quality postgraduate research related to heritage conservation and management, sustainable development and artificial intelligence, with particular attention to interdisciplinary research connecting these themes with social, ethical, governance and contextual dimensions. Through research stays in Japanese universities and research institutions, fellows will have the opportunity to further develop their work and engage with Japan’s academic and research community. Cycle 2026 at a glance Key information Details Fellowships available 10 Fellowship grant Up to US$10,000 Duration No less than 3 months and no more than 9 months Host country Japan Fellowship period in Japan From February 2027 onwards, to be completed no later than December 2027. Application deadline 30 September 2026, midnight Paris time Submission channel Through National Commissions for UNESCO Invited Member States and Associate Members AFRICA – 47 Member States: Angola, Benin, Botswana, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon, Cabo Verde, Central African Republic, Chad, Comoros, Congo, Cote d’Ivoire, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Djibouti, Equatorial Guinea, Eritrea, Eswatini, Ethiopia, Gabon, Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mali, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, Niger, Nigeria, Rwanda, Sao Tome and Principe, Senegal, Seychelles, Sierra Leone, Somalia, South Africa, South Sudan, Togo, Uganda, United Republic of Tanzania, Zambia, Zimbabwe ARAB STATES – 1 Member State: Bahrain ASIA AND THE PACIFIC – 17 Member States, 2 Associate Members*: Cook Islands, Fiji, Kiribati, Maldives, Marshall Islands, Micronesia (Federated State of), Nauru, Niue, New Caledonia*, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Singapore, Solomon Islands, Timor-Leste, Tokelau*, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN – 16 Member States, 7 Associate Members*: Anguilla*, Antigua and Barbuda, Aruba*, Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, British Virgin Islands*, Cayman Islands*, Cuba, Curaçao*, Dominica, Dominican Republic, Grenada, Guyana, Haiti, Jamaica, Montserrat*, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Sint Maarten*, Suriname, Trinidad and Tobago EUROPE – 2 Member States: Türkiye, Ukraine Research areas Research proposals submitted under the 2026 cycle should fall within one of the following research areas. Applicants should refer to Annex 2 for the full list of indicative sub-areas and select one primary research area and one corresponding sub-area that best reflect the focus of their proposed research. Heritage Conservation and Management (4 sub-areas) AI for Sustainable Management of Natural Resources and Climate Action （5 sub-areas) Ethical, Inclusive, and Human Centred AI for Sustainable Development (6 sub-areas) AI for Sustainable Cities, Infrastructure, and Societal Resilience (6 sub-areas) AI and Education (7 sub-areas) Eligibility requirements Applicants must: be nationals of one of the invited Member States or Associate Members listed in Annex 1 ; be no more than 40 years old at the time of application; hold at least a Master’s degree or equivalent in a field relevant to the proposed research and demonstrate strong academic and research potential; demonstrate sufficient proficiency in reading and writing in the language of instruction or supervision at the proposed host institution in Japan; have obtained acceptance from an academic supervisor at a Japanese university or research institution, who will oversee the proposed research. Fellowship grant and eligible costs Selected fellows may receive a fellowship grant of up to US$10,000. The grant will be provided as a lump-sum contribution and is intended to cover costs directly related to the approved research stay in Japan. The grant may cover: international and domestic travel for the approved itinerary; accommodation; medical insurance; personal subsistence in Japan, including meals, local transportation and incidental expenses; other research-related expenses, where applicable. The grant does not cover tuition fees, the purchase of equipment, including computers, publication costs or participation in conferences, unless such participation can be clearly justified as an integral part of the research and makes a direct and significant contribution to the project. Medical insurance is mandatory for all selected fellows and will be arranged by UNESCO on their behalf. The cost of medical insurance will be deducted from the total fellowship amount before disbursement. How to apply Step 1 : Read carefully the Application Guide to understand the requirements for eligible candidatures and the procedures for the submission of application. Step 2: Contact the National Commission for UNESCO of your home country to enquire about the application procedures at the national level. Click here for the contact information of the National Commissions for UNESCO. Step 3: Prepare all required documents, including the application form ( Annex 3 ), academic documents, recommendation letter, host institution acceptance letter, language certificate and research proposal ( Annex 4 ). Step 4: Submit your application to the National Commission for UNESCO of your home country, at least 2 weeks before the required deadline . Step 5 : As soon as you are informed by the National Commission for UNESCO of your country that you are nominated as a candidate for this programme, you should communicate your the online application form and the supporting documents to keizoobuchi.fellowships@unesco.org . Note: Only applications nominated by the National Commission will be accepted by UNESCO. Step 6: Letters of nomination, along with all the application documents should be submitted to UNESCO by the National Commissions no later than 30 September 2026, midnight Paris time . Candidates who submit incomplete applications, or submit the online applications beyond this deadline won t be considered. Selection process Applications will be evaluated by a Selection Committee composed of experts from UNESCO and the Government of Japan in the relevant fields. The evaluation will take into account the merits of the candidates and the quality, relevance and originality of their proposed research. The final selection decision will be made by the Japanese authorities, based on the recommendation of the Committee, with due consideration to gender equality and diversity. Source: https://www.unesco.org/en/fellowships/keizo-obuchi The post UNESCO/Japan Young Researchers’ Fellowships Programme 2026: Up to US$10,000 for Research in Japan appeared first on Opportunities for Youth .

title: Global Child Health (GCH) Fellowship Program 2027 at SickKids, Canada
summary: The Centre for Global Child Health (CGCH) at The Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids) in Toronto, Canada, is inviting applications for the Global Child Health (GCH) Fellowship Program. This prestigious fellowship is designed for professionals who are passionate about improving child health outcomes around the world through research, leadership, innovation, and capacity building. The fellowship offers an outstanding opportunity for individuals from diverse healthcare and research backgrounds to develop the skills needed to become leaders in global child health. Participants will work alongside internationally recognized researchers and practitioners while contributing to projects that address some of the world s most pressing child health challenges. About the Global Child Health Fellowship Program The Global Child Health Fellowship Program is a comprehensive two-year interdisciplinary training program that prepares fellows for impactful careers in global health. Rather than focusing solely on academic learning, the program combines practical experience with leadership development. Fellows become actively involved in the design, implementation, analysis, and evaluation of research and capacity-building initiatives that improve health systems and child well-being worldwide. Hosted by the Centre for Global Child Health at SickKids, one of the world s leading pediatric hospitals, the fellowship provides an exceptional learning environment where fellows collaborate with experts addressing complex global health issues. Fellowship Objectives The program aims to prepare the next generation of global health leaders by helping fellows: Build advanced leadership skills. Strengthen research capacity. Develop expertise in implementation science. Improve project management and evaluation skills. Contribute to innovative global health initiatives. Support health system strengthening in low- and middle-income countries. Enhance collaboration across multidisciplinary teams. Research Areas Fellows may contribute to projects covering a wide range of global child health topics, including: Nutrition Child growth and development Pediatric oncology Infectious diseases Climate change and child health Microbiome research Vaccine development Complex systems and network science Implementation science Health systems strengthening Health workforce training Capacity building initiatives Other emerging global health priorities This broad range of research themes allows fellows to gain practical experience while addressing real-world health challenges affecting children globally. Fellowship Duration The fellowship runs for two years . During this period, fellows will participate in interdisciplinary research, leadership training, scholarly development, and collaborative projects under the mentorship of experienced global health professionals. Who Can Apply For This Fellowship Opportunity ? The fellowship welcomes applicants from a wide variety of educational and professional backgrounds. Eligible applicants may include professionals in fields such as: Medicine (MD) Doctoral graduates (PhD) Nursing Allied Health Professions Public Health Health Research Other relevant healthcare disciplines Individuals with a strong commitment to improving child health through research, education, implementation science, or capacity building are encouraged to apply. Why Apply? Participating in the Global Child Health Fellowship Program provides numerous professional and academic benefits, including: Training at one of Canada s leading pediatric research institutions. Mentorship from internationally recognized global health experts. Leadership development opportunities. Hands-on experience in global health research. Exposure to interdisciplinary collaborations. Opportunities to contribute to high-impact projects. Professional networking with researchers and health professionals from around the world. Preparation for long-term careers in global health research and policy. Application Process Interested applicants should review the official fellowship information and complete the online application before the deadline. Applicants are encouraged to prepare all required documents well in advance to avoid last-minute delays. Application Portal Apply for this opportunity HERE Important Dates Application Deadline : September 13, 2026 (11:59 p.m. EDT) Expected Fellowship Start : On or before July 2, 2027 Contact Applicants with questions regarding the fellowship may contact the Global Child Health Fellowship Program Committee through the official contact information provided by SickKids. Conclusion The Global Child Health Fellowship Program at SickKids offers an exceptional opportunity for healthcare professionals and researchers seeking to make a meaningful impact on child health worldwide. Through world-class mentorship, interdisciplinary collaboration, leadership training, and involvement in transformative research projects, fellows will gain the expertise needed to address global child health challenges. If you aspire to become a leader in global health research or capacity building, this fellowship represents an excellent pathway toward achieving that goal. Interested applicants should submit their applications before September 13, 2026 , to be considered for this highly competitive program. title: Africa CDC Youth Public Health & Digital Health Research Training Workshop 2026 for Young African Professionals
summary: Young African professionals interested in public health, digital health, research, and healthcare innovation are invited to join the Africa CDC Youth Public Health Digital Health Research Training Workshop 2026 , a three-day virtual hands-on training taking place from 27–29 July 2026 . The training will bring together 100 young professionals from across Africa to strengthen their practical skills in research design, research methodology, and concept note development . Key Details Program: Public Health Digital Health Research Training Workshop 2026 Dates: 27–29 July 2026 Duration: 3 days Format: Virtual Participants: 100 young professionals from across Africa Eligibility: Exclusively for members of the Africa Youths in Digital Health Network (YiDHN) Focus Areas: Research design, research methodology, and concept note development Collaboration: West African Institute of Public Health Network: Africa Youths in Digital Health Network (YiDHN), an initiative under the Africa CDC Youth Program Join YiDHN: https://bit.ly/join_yidhn About the Africa CDC Youth Public Health Digital Health Research Training Workshop 2026 The Public Health Digital Health Research Training Workshop 2026 is designed to equip young African professionals with practical skills to strengthen their capacity to conduct research and contribute to innovation in public and digital health. Taking place virtually from 27 to 29 July 2026 , the three-day hands-on workshop will provide participants with practical knowledge in research design, research methodology, and the development of strong concept notes. Organized in collaboration with the West African Institute of Public Health , the training will bring together 100 young professionals from across Africa , creating an opportunity to build research capacity, foster collaboration, and advance digital health innovation across the continent. What Will Participants Learn? The training will focus on three core areas: Research Design: Strengthening participants ability to develop structured and relevant research approaches. Research Methodology: Building practical knowledge of methods and approaches for conducting effective research. Concept Note Development: Developing the skills needed to prepare clear and compelling research concept notes. Participants will also have the opportunity to connect with other young professionals interested in public health, digital health, research, technology, and healthcare innovation across Africa. Who Can Participate? The Public Health Digital Health Research Training Workshop is exclusively for members of the Africa Youths in Digital Health Network (YiDHN) . The workshop will accommodate 100 young professionals from across Africa who are interested in strengthening their research capacity and contributing to digital health innovation. Those who are not yet members of YiDHN can join the network through the onboarding form. About the Africa Youths in Digital Health Network (YiDHN) The Africa Youths in Digital Health Network (YiDHN) is an initiative under the Africa CDC Youth Program aimed at empowering young professionals across Africa to lead the transformation of healthcare through digital solutions. The network brings together young people passionate about digital health and provides opportunities to connect, build capacity, collaborate, and contribute to shaping the future of healthcare in Africa. Through the network, young professionals can also gain access to future training, mentorship, networking, and capacity-building opportunities . Why Join the YiDHN? Africa s rapidly evolving digital health landscape creates significant opportunities for young professionals to contribute to healthcare transformation through research, technology, innovation, and collaboration. By joining YiDHN, young professionals can become part of a growing continental network focused on fostering innovation, building capacity, and driving impactful change in digital health across Africa . Membership also provides an avenue to learn about opportunities such as the Public Health Digital Health Research Training Workshop and future initiatives for young digital health professionals. How to Join the Africa Youths in Digital Health Network Interested young professionals can complete the Africa Youths in Digital Health Network (YiDHN) Onboarding Form to join the network. Join the YiDHN here: https://bit.ly/join_yidhn Join a community of young African professionals working to advance digital health innovation, research, capacity building, and healthcare transformation across Africa . title: The World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) Fellowship 2026 in Geneva, Switzerland | CHF 6,000 Monthly Stipend | Open Worldwide
summary: The World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) is offering a Fellowship opportunity with the WIPO Knowledge Center (WKC) in Geneva, Switzerland. The fellowship has a contract duration of 12 months, with the possibility to renew, and provides a monthly stipend of CHF 6,000. Key Details Organization: World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) Eligibility: Open to applicants worldwide who meet the requirements. Fellowship: Fellowship 26229-FEL Section: WIPO Knowledge Center, IP Futures and Knowledge Management Section, Administration, Finance and Management Sector Duty Station: CH-Geneva Location: WIPO Headquarters, Geneva, Switzerland Contract Duration: 12 months Stipend: CHF 6,000 monthly Anticipated Start Date: October 1, 2026 Publication Date: 22-Jul-2026 Application Deadline: 06-Aug-2026, 10:59:00 PM Grade: N/A IMPORTANT NOTICE REGARDING APPLICATION DEADLINE: Please note that the deadline for applications is indicated in local time as per the time zone of the applicant s location. 1. Organizational context (a) Organizational Setting The World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) is a United Nations specialized agency. Its WIPO Knowledge Center (WKC) is the custodian of the knowledge repository, which is an authoritative source for global IP academic research. The WKC oversees WIPO’s physical and digital library collection, in addition to the dissemination of WIPO publications. The WKC team requires a qualified Fellow to support the library and knowledge services by collecting, analyzing, and reporting data that informs evidence-based decision-making. Working closely with colleagues, the fellow will contribute to the assessment of library services, digital resources, and user engagement, helping to identify opportunities to improve discoverability, accessibility, and service delivery. Fellowships aim to provide fellows with experience to strengthen their knowledge and professional competence, which they can apply in their professional field once they have completed their fellowship with WIPO. (b) Reporting Lines The Fellow shall work under the supervision of the Head of the WIPO Knowledge Center (WKC). (c) Objectives During the fellowship, the Fellow will assist with the WKC activities and gain in-depth knowledge and competence in the respective field. 2. Duties and responsibilities The Fellow will provide support in the following areas: a) Collect, validate, and manage quantitative and qualitative data relating to library services, digital collections, and information resources. b) Gather, monitor, and analyze usage statistics from library platforms, repositories, websites, and other digital services. c) Produce regular statistical reports to support strategic planning and operational decision-making. d) Analyze trends in resource usage, identifying patterns and opportunities for improvement. e) Assist in developing and maintaining key performance indicators (KPIs) for library services and digital initiatives. f) Contribute to the evaluation of digital resources, collections, and services using evidence-based assessment techniques. g) Assist in collecting and analyzing citation, bibliometric, altmetric, and other research impact data, where applicable. f) Prepare reports, presentations, and briefing materials summarizing analytical findings for internal stakeholders. h) Collaborate with colleagues to improve workflows for data collection, reporting, and assessment. i) Perform other related duties as required. 3. Requirements (a) Education Essential: At least a first-level degree in library, information science, knowledge management or a related field. Recognized professional qualification. (b) Experience Essential: At least two years of professional experience working in a library, knowledge management, research support, or related environment. Experience collecting, managing, and analyzing library or information-related data. Experience working with usage statistics, service metrics, or other performance data to support assessment activities. Experience preparing analytical reports and presenting findings to support decision-making. Experience using spreadsheet software and data analysis tools. Desirable: Experience working with integrated library systems, institutional repositories, discovery platforms, or digital library services. Experience using business intelligence, dashboard, or data visualization tools. Experience working with bibliometric, altmetric, or research impact indicators. Experience with SQL, Python, R, or other analytical tools would be an advantage. (c) Languages Essential: Excellent (written and spoken) knowledge of English. Desirable: Good knowledge of at least one of WIPO s other official languages would be an advantage. (d) Specific skills and competencies Essential: Sound understanding of library operations and digital information services. Knowledge of library assessment methodologies and performance measurement. Ability to collect, clean, organize, and interpret data from multiple sources. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with excellent attention to detail. Ability to identify trends and communicate findings clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences. Good understanding of statistical concepts and data visualization principles. Ability to work independently while contributing effectively within a collaborative team. Excellent written and oral communication skills. 4. Organizational competencies Communicating effectively. Showing team spirit. Demonstrating integrity. Valuing diversity. Producing results. Showing service orientation. Seeing the big picture. Seeking change and innovation. Developing yourself and others. 5. Terms and conditions a) Term of fellowship: A fellowship may be granted for a period of up to 12 months with the possibility to renew. b) Anticipated Start Date: October 1, 2026. c) Location: WIPO Headquarters, Geneva, Switzerland. d) Stipend: CHF 6,000 monthly. e) Travel expenses: WIPO shall contribute towards the cost of the fellow’s travel on engagement and separation from service. If necessary, WIPO may provide assistance in obtaining an entry visa to Switzerland. f) WIPO contributes towards the medical insurance and provides accident insurance coverage during the course of the fellowship. g) WIPO will request a “carte de legitimation” for the Fellow, which serves as a residence and work permit, from the Permanent Mission of Switzerland to the United Nations Office and to the other international organizations in Geneva. Family members of the Fellow are not eligible for a “carte de legitimation.” h) Tax and social security: Fellows shall be solely responsible for meeting any taxation and social security obligations that may arise directly or indirectly from their contract with WIPO. The list can be accessed through the link: http://www.whed.net/ . Some professional certificates may not appear in the WHED and these will be reviewed individually. Additional testing/interviewing may be used as a form of screening. Initial appointment is subject to satisfactory professional references. title: International Online School in Forced Migration 2026–2027: Apply for the World-Renowned Refugee Studies Centre Online Programme
summary: Forced migration, displacement, and refugee protection remain among the most urgent global issues of the 21st century. As conflict, climate change, political instability, and humanitarian crises continue to force millions of people from their homes, there is an increasing need for professionals, researchers, policymakers, humanitarian workers, and advocates who understand the complexities of forced migration and can contribute to evidence-based solutions. To meet this growing need, the Refugee Studies Centre (RSC) is once again offering its internationally recognized International Online School in Forced Migration during the 2026–2027 academic year. Widely regarded as one of the world s leading educational programmes in the field, the Online School provides participants with an exceptional opportunity to deepen their understanding of forced migration through rigorous academic study, expert-led discussions, and global networking. Designed specifically for busy professionals, academics, researchers, and policymakers, the programme combines flexible online learning with live interactive sessions, allowing participants to engage with world-renowned scholars without having to leave their workplace or country. Why the International Online School in Forced Migration Matters Forced migration affects millions of people worldwide due to armed conflict, persecution, environmental disasters, climate change, political instability, and violations of human rights. At the same time, many governments are adopting increasingly restrictive migration policies, reducing protection for displaced populations and limiting opportunities for safe movement. These challenges demand informed leadership, critical thinking, and multidisciplinary approaches. However, professionals working in humanitarian response, migration policy, refugee protection, and related fields often have limited opportunities for structured learning and reflection. The Refugee Studies Centre s International Online School addresses this gap by creating an intensive academic environment where participants can: Develop a deeper understanding of forced migration. Examine contemporary refugee issues from multiple perspectives. Learn directly from internationally respected experts. Exchange experiences with professionals from around the world. Build lasting professional relationships across sectors. Programme Dates Due to increasing global demand, the Refugee Studies Centre will offer the International Online School twice during the 2026–2027 academic year. First Session: 7–11 December 2026 Second Session: 21–25 June 2027 Participants may choose the session that best fits their professional schedule. About the Refugee Studies Centre The Refugee Studies Centre (RSC) is internationally recognized for excellence in research, teaching, and policy engagement on forced migration. Its International Online School reflects the Centre s commitment to: Academic excellence Evidence-based research Inclusive teaching Critical thinking Interdisciplinary learning Practical relevance The programme has earned an outstanding global reputation among humanitarian professionals, researchers, international organizations, NGOs, government agencies, and universities. What Participants Will Learn The programme explores forced migration from a wide range of academic and practical perspectives rather than focusing on a single discipline. Participants gain insights into topics such as: Refugee protection Forced displacement International migration Humanitarian response Refugee law Human rights Climate-induced displacement Conflict and displacement Migration governance Social integration Policy development Humanitarian ethics Global migration trends Evidence-based approaches to migration research The curriculum encourages participants to think critically about the many interconnected factors that shape migration experiences worldwide. Flexible Online Learning Structure The programme is carefully designed to accommodate working professionals. Before the live teaching week begins, participants receive access to: Pre-recorded lectures Assigned readings Learning exercises Preparatory materials These resources allow participants to build foundational knowledge before joining live sessions. During the scheduled programme week, participants engage in: Live seminars Interactive discussions Expert lectures Academic debates Collaborative learning activities This blended approach combines flexibility with real-time interaction, ensuring participants benefit from both self-paced study and direct engagement with leading scholars. Learn from Leading Experts One of the programme s strongest features is access to internationally recognized experts working across the fields of: Refugee studies International law Anthropology Political science Sociology Humanitarian action Development studies Human rights Migration policy Participants benefit from diverse academic perspectives while also learning from practitioners with extensive field experience. Networking Opportunities Beyond the academic curriculum, the International Online School provides valuable networking opportunities. Participants connect with: Researchers Humanitarian professionals NGO leaders Government officials Policy experts International organization staff Graduate students Academics Networking activities are designed to encourage meaningful conversations, collaboration, and long-term professional relationships. Many participants report that these global connections remain valuable long after the programme concludes. Learning Environment The Refugee Studies Centre emphasizes an educational environment that is: Inclusive Respectful Research-driven Interactive Multidisciplinary Globally diverse Rather than promoting advocacy alone, the programme encourages participants to examine forced migration through careful analysis, evidence, and scholarly debate. What Makes This Programme Unique? Several characteristics distinguish the International Online School from many other migration programmes. 1. International Reputation The programme is recognized worldwide as one of the leading educational events focused on forced migration. 2. Academic Excellence Participants receive rigorous, evidence-based instruction delivered by internationally respected scholars. 3. Practical Relevance The curriculum connects academic research with real-world humanitarian and policy challenges. 4. Flexible Online Format Participants can study from anywhere while balancing work and other commitments. 5. Global Networking The programme attracts participants from diverse countries, professions, and backgrounds. 6. Interdisciplinary Perspective Rather than focusing solely on legal or humanitarian issues, the programme explores historical, political, anthropological, psychological, and social dimensions of displacement. Participant Testimonials Previous participants consistently describe the programme as transformative. Highlights from participant experiences include: Learning from world-leading scholars and practitioners. Developing a deeper understanding of migration through rigorous academic discussion. Gaining fresh perspectives that challenge existing assumptions. Exploring migration through historical, anthropological, legal, psychosocial, and policy lenses. Building meaningful relationships with professionals from around the world. Participating in intellectually stimulating discussions that extend beyond everyday professional responsibilities. Appreciating an inclusive learning environment that promotes reflection, dialogue, and evidence-based thinking. Participants also praise the programme for encouraging thoughtful scholarship rather than simplistic approaches to complex migration issues. Click HERE to read more. Who Should Attend? The International Online School is ideal for individuals working in or interested in: Refugee protection Humanitarian assistance Migration policy International development Human rights Government agencies International organizations NGOs Academia Research institutions Legal practice Public policy Social sciences Students seeking advanced knowledge in migration studies may also benefit from participating. How to Apply Interested applicants should visit the official programme page to review complete programme information, eligibility requirements, tuition details, and registration procedures. Applicants are encouraged to apply early to secure their place in their preferred session. APPLY HERE Conclusion The International Online School in Forced Migration 2026–2027 offers a unique opportunity for professionals, researchers, students, and policymakers to strengthen their expertise in one of today s most pressing global issues. Combining academic excellence, internationally recognized faculty, flexible online learning, and a diverse global community of participants, the programme equips learners with the knowledge, critical thinking skills, and professional networks needed to better understand and respond to forced migration and refugee challenges. title: Call for Applications: The V20 Climate Prosperity Fellowship Program (2026-2027)
summary: OVERVIEW In 2023, the CVF-V20 and the Boston University Global Development Policy Center launched the V20 Climate Prosperity Fellowship Program for finance officials (or equivalent) from CVF-V20 Member Countries. The Fellowship Program is an integral part of the CVF-V20’s ongoing efforts to promote and drive ambitious climate action and to mobilize international support for climate vulnerable nations. The aim of the V20 Climate Prosperity Fellowship Program is to engender cooperation among CVF-V20 member states, provide them with the tools to combat challenges they may face in the pursuit of strategies to avert climate breakdown, and pioneer the development of economic and financial solutions, including the mobilization of domestic climate finance towards positive climate action. The V20 Climate Prosperity Fellowship Program is designed to provide mid- to senior career officials with opportunities for peer-learning, building cutting-edge technical skills to integrate climate change into their work, and supporting their leadership in advancing innovative solutions. The CVF-V20 has consistently emphasized the need to reform the international financial architecture to unlock opportunities on the ground to promote climate prosperity. Through weekly webinars, interactions with experts, residencies, and immersive exercises, V20 Climate Prosperity Fellows will have a unique opportunity to work together in advancing a fit for purpose international financial architecture. COLLABORATION OBJECTIVES At the end of the program, Fellows are expected to be well positioned to support resource mobilization for Climate Prosperity Plans and to: Understand the international financial architecture and be able to identify opportunities to support climate prosperity; Engage in policy discussions concerning reform of the international financial architecture; Harness the knowledge and skills needed to engage and access processes associated with the international financial architecture, including on debt reform, shifting of financial flows, carbon financing exchanges, and mainstream surveillance of climate risks to drive new investment; Identify and deploy communications strategies used to raise awareness of the priorities of the climate-vulnerable countries in relation to the reform of the international financial architecture; and Contribute to the formulation and implementation of their countries’ Climate Prosperity Plans. TARGET OUTCOME To provide peer-learning and technical enhancement support to the finance ministries (or equivalent) of 16 to 20 CVF-V20 member countries by equipping Fellows with skills to pursue the mobilization of financial resources more effectively to support ambitious national climate prosperity plans for development positive climate action. KEY ACTIVITIES Participation in online classes/seminars/workshops; Participation in one-week in-person residencies in January 2027 and October 2027; Participation in relevant meetings, supported by the CVF-V20; Participation in interactive discussions with representatives of International Financial Institutions and partner groups with the support of the CVF-V20; and Preparation and delivery of presentations during V20 Senior Officials Meetings and relevant CVF-V20 workshops and events. CONDITIONS OF PARTICIPATION Candidates from Ministries of Finance (or equivalent) in CVF-V20 member countries who meet the requirements set out below are invited to apply to participate in the year-long Fellowship Program for the period 2026- 2027: Citizen of a CVF-V20 member country; Official with demonstrated five to ten years of mid- to senior-level experience in international affairs, public policy and/or development, including climate/environmental/sustainable development; Committed to participate in the Fellowship program’s activities organized throughout the year, both online and in-person and to complete and submit assignments as required; Willingness to travel abroad to attend in person meetings and training sessions with members of their cohort; Commitment to attend scheduled weekly virtual sessions for the duration of the fellowship period; Committed to working and sharing information with their national government and national stakeholders after the completion of the Fellowship; Committed to integrating into the growing network of V20 CPP fellows and staying engaged in the community to advance common priorities and mutual learning; and Proﬁcient in English. *Prospective Fellows interested in undertaking intensive training in debt sustainability analyses should indicate the same in their application and, in so doing, commit to an additional session to undertake this training each week. Proficiency in using Microsoft Excel and familiarity with macroeconomic concepts are recommended. APPLICATION PROCESS Interested officials must submit their application by accomplishing the form: Submit your application here The deadline for submission of applications is on 31 July 2026. TENTATIVE FELLOWSHIP TIMELINE Month August 2026 Selection and notification of Fellows September 2026 Finance Ministries (or equivalent) provide official confirmation of selected Fellows’ participation in the Program October 2026 Weekly webinars begin and continue throughout the year January 2027 First in-person residency *Location will be confirmed in due course January 2027 Proposals for capstone projects submitted for feedback March 2027 Fellows provide inputs to the V20 Senior Officials Meeting March 2027 Virtual Meeting Fellows contribute to preparations for the Spring Meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank Group, including through the identification of priorities, policy goals, and strategies with the goal to put together a singular document for Spring Meetings priorities, with the possibility of sharing externally, as well as to the V20 Communiqué. April 2027 2027 Spring Meetings of the IMF and the World Bank Group Fellows contribute to the hybrid sessions on topics relevant to the CVF-V20 Virtual or in-person participation during the 18th V20 Ministerial Dialogue October 2027 Second in-person residency *Location will be confirmed in due course Presentation of final capstone projects Conclusion of the program and graduation KEY CONTACTS For additional information about the program and application process, please contact: Christian F. Soqueño Deputy Director for Fellowships, Membership and Partnerships Coordination +63 9175932773 christian.soqueno@cvfv20.org Farrah Brown Diplomacy Lead, Membership and Partnerships Coordination +1 9175269281 farrah.brown@cvfv20.org CVF-V20 Secretariat secretariat@cvfv20.org Source: https://cvfv20.org/call-for-applications-the-v20-climate-prosperity-fellowship-program-2026-2027/ The post Call for Applications: The V20 Climate Prosperity Fellowship Program (2026-2027) appeared first on Opportunities for Youth .

title: UNDP Call for Proposals 2026: Funding Opportunity for CSOs and NGOs to End Violence Against Women and Girls in Africa
summary: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Ethiopia has announced a Call for Proposals for Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and NGOs under the Spotlight Initiative Africa Regional Programme (SIARP) 2.0 to End Violence Against Women and Girls (EVAWG) . This opportunity invites eligible civil society organizations to submit proposals to contribute to efforts aimed at ending violence against women and girls across Africa. The initiative provides an opportunity for organizations working on gender equality, women s rights, prevention of gender-based violence, advocacy, community engagement, and related areas to participate in a major regional programme. Applications must be submitted through the UNDP Quantum Supplier Portal by 29 July 2026 at 4:00 AM New York time . About the UNDP Call for Proposals The call is managed by UNDP Ethiopia and relates to the Spotlight Initiative Africa Regional Programme (SIARP) 2.0 to End Violence Against Women and Girls (EVAWG) . The programme seeks to support efforts to address violence against women and girls through collaboration with civil society organizations and other partners. Opportunity at a Glance Organization: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Office: UNDP Ethiopia Programme: Spotlight Initiative Africa Regional Programme (SIARP) 2.0 Focus: Ending Violence Against Women and Girls (EVAWG) Contract Type: Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) Duty Station: Home-based Programme Duration: August 2026 – December 2028 Expected Start Date: Upon signing of the agreement Application Deadline: 29 July 2026 at 4:00 AM New York time Reference Number: UNDP-ETH-00754 Contact: info.procurementet@undp.org Who Can Apply? The call is specifically targeted at Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) . Organizations interested in applying should carefully review the official solicitation and negotiation documents available through the UNDP Quantum Supplier Portal to determine the full eligibility, technical, administrative, and documentation requirements. Applicants should ensure that the organization name entered during supplier registration is the full legal name corresponding with the organization s legal and bank account records . About the Spotlight Initiative Africa Regional Programme 2.0 The services under this call relate to the Spotlight Initiative Africa Regional Programme (SIARP) 2.0 to End Violence Against Women and Girls (EVAWG) . The programme focuses on efforts to address violence against women and girls in Africa and strengthen action toward gender equality and women s rights. Civil society organizations have an important role in this work, including through community engagement, advocacy, prevention, service delivery, accountability, and advancing the rights and agency of women and girls. Applicants should consult the official tender documents for the precise scope of work, expected results, deliverables, eligibility criteria, and proposal requirements. Contract Duration and Location The assignment is expected to run from August 2026 through December 2028 , with the agreement commencing upon signing. The duty station is listed as home-based , making this a particularly relevant opportunity for qualifying organizations capable of contributing to the programme s regional objectives without being based at a UNDP office. How to Apply for the UNDP CSO Call for Proposals Applications must be submitted electronically through the UNDP Quantum Supplier Portal . Interested organizations should: Register on the UNDP Quantum Supplier Portal if they do not already have a supplier profile. If already registered, log in using the existing supplier account. Do not create another profile. Search for the negotiation using reference number UNDP-ETH-00754 . Subscribe to the tender to receive notifications about amendments or updates. Create a draft response in the system to indicate your intention to submit a proposal. This enables UNDP to send relevant notifications if the tender requirements are amended. Review all negotiation and solicitation documents carefully before preparing the application. Submit the complete offer directly through the Quantum Supplier Portal before the deadline. Organizations that have previously registered but cannot remember their login details should use the forgotten password/username functionality rather than creating a new account. Organizations should also subscribe to the tender after locating it in Quantum. This is important because UNDP may issue amendments, clarifications, or updates before the submission deadline. Interested CSOs are strongly encouraged to begin the registration and application process early to allow sufficient time to review the solicitation documents and resolve any supplier portal issues. Application Deadline The deadline for submissions is: 29 July 2026 at 4:00 AM (New York time). Applications must be submitted directly through the UNDP Quantum Supplier Portal in accordance with the requirements of the solicitation. Given the deadline, prospective applicants should review the opportunity and begin preparing their submissions as soon as possible. Official Application and Further Information Tender Reference: UNDP-ETH-00754 Application Portal: UNDP Quantum Supplier Portal UNDP Resources for Bidders: Applicants can consult UNDP s procurement resources for guidance on supplier registration, using the Quantum system, and submitting bids. Procurement Office: UNDP Ethiopia Procurement Unit Contact Email: info.procurementet@undp.org Applicants should rely on the official UNDP procurement notice and solicitation documents for the definitive eligibility criteria, requirements, deadlines, and application instructions. title: Roosevelt Institute Good Life Residents Program 2026: Fully Funded Remote Fellowship Offering $3,000 Stipend for Emerging Economic Policy Leaders
summary: The Roosevelt Institute is inviting experienced policy professionals, researchers, academics, and experts to apply for the Good Life Residents Program 2026 , a prestigious six-month remote residency designed to cultivate innovative policy leaders and generate transformative ideas that advance economic justice in the United States. As part of the Roosevelt Institute s broader Good Life Agenda , selected residents will work alongside leading economists, policy experts, researchers, and senior advisors to develop original policy proposals addressing some of the country s most pressing economic challenges. Participants will produce policy essays, collaborate with subject matter experts, contribute to national policy conversations, and receive $3,000 in compensation , along with travel and accommodation support for the program s concluding event if required. One of the featured residency tracks is the AI and Finance Residents Program , created in partnership with Data Society , which focuses on examining how artificial intelligence is transforming finance, investment, labor markets, industrial policy, and the broader economy. This residency provides an outstanding opportunity for experienced professionals who are passionate about shaping public policy, promoting equitable economic growth, and influencing the future of AI governance. About the Roosevelt Institute Good Life Residents Program The Good Life Residents Program is a six-month policy residency that brings together a small cohort of emerging and established policy thinkers to explore solutions aligned with the Roosevelt Institute s vision for a stronger and more equitable economy. Rather than conducting traditional academic research, residents focus on producing practical, people-centered policy ideas that can influence public debate and policymaking. The program emphasizes collaboration, mentorship, public engagement, and intellectual exchange. Throughout the residency, participants work closely with: Roosevelt Institute Think Tank directors Senior organizational leadership Topic advisors Fellow residents Policy practitioners Academic experts Organizers and government leaders Each residency concludes with a public event designed to amplify participants ideas and encourage dialogue on important national and state-level policy issues. AI and Finance Residents Program One of the Roosevelt Institute s featured residency topics explores the rapidly evolving relationship between artificial intelligence and finance. Massive investments in generative AI have significantly reshaped the economy, influencing: Stock markets Financial markets Corporate profits Bond issuance Employment trends Industrial development Trade policy Technology investment Economic growth Today, just seven technology companies account for more than one-third of the total market capitalization of the S P 500, raising concerns about market concentration, financial stability, and economic inequality. The Roosevelt Institute, together with Data Society , seeks residents capable of producing bold policy ideas that help redirect AI investment toward broader public benefit while protecting workers, strengthening democratic institutions, and encouraging sustainable innovation. Objectives of the AI and Finance Residency The residency seeks to answer important policy questions such as: How can governments better oversee private AI investments? How can policymakers reduce excessive concentration within the technology sector? How can AI investment benefit society rather than only large corporations? How can governments encourage investment across other important sectors of the economy? How should AI policy balance innovation, public safety, labor protections, and national competitiveness? What democratic institutions are needed to ensure accountability over public investments in AI? How can governments support technology research that strengthens supply chains and sustainability? Participants are encouraged to propose original, practical, and people-centered policy recommendations. What Residents Will Do Successful applicants will participate in numerous activities throughout the six-month residency. These include: Develop Original Policy Essays Residents will research and write an approximately 1,500-word policy essay presenting innovative solutions aligned with the Roosevelt Institute s Good Life Agenda. Each essay responds to a specific policy prompt within the resident s assigned topic area. Join a Small Collaborative Cohort Each topic area consists of only three to four residents , creating an environment that encourages meaningful collaboration, peer learning, and intellectual exchange. Residents will work closely with one another throughout the program. Work with Expert Advisors Every cohort is supported by one or two Topic Advisors. These advisors include: Leading academics Government practitioners Policy leaders Organizers Industry experts They provide: Intellectual mentorship Strategic guidance Feedback on policy proposals Moderation during discussions and public events Participate in Public Events At the end of the residency, participants present and discuss their policy ideas during a public event organized by the Roosevelt Institute. The event helps amplify participants work while encouraging national dialogue around economic policy. Contribute to Public Engagement Residents may also participate in: Opinion editorials (Op-Eds) Press interviews Reporter briefings Public policy discussions Media engagement opportunities Serve as Good Life Agenda Ambassadors Participants are expected to promote and represent the Roosevelt Institute s Good Life Agenda throughout their professional and public networks. Program Structure Each residency topic includes: 3–4 Good Life Residents 1–2 senior Topic Advisors Roosevelt Institute policy staff Organizational leadership support The program emphasizes mentorship, collaboration, and practical policy development. Program Duration The residency lasts: Six months Time Commitment Residents should expect to dedicate approximately: 5–8 hours per month This makes the residency suitable for professionals balancing existing work or academic responsibilities. Location The program is primarily: Remote However, participants may be invited to travel for selected meetings or the final public event. Compensation Selected residents will receive: $3,000 stipend Travel expenses covered (if required) Accommodation for the concluding event (if required) This financial support enables participants to fully engage in the residency while contributing meaningful policy work. Who Should Apply? The Roosevelt Institute encourages applications from individuals with substantial experience in policy development, technology, economics, or related fields. Ideal applicants include: Policy professionals Researchers Economists Academics Government practitioners Technology policy experts AI researchers Industrial policy specialists Think tank professionals Candidates should demonstrate both subject expertise and a commitment to developing policies that improve economic outcomes for society. Required Qualifications Successful applicants should have: Demonstrated expertise in artificial intelligence, technology policy, industrial policy, or a related discipline. A minimum of five years of professional or academic policy experience . Strong analytical and writing abilities. An interest in advancing equitable economic policy. The ability to collaborate within multidisciplinary teams. A commitment to contributing original policy ideas. Benefits of Joining the Program Participants will enjoy numerous professional benefits, including: $3,000 financial compensation. National exposure through public events. Collaboration with leading policy experts. Individual mentorship from senior advisors. Opportunity to publish original policy work. Professional networking opportunities. Media and press engagement. Flexible remote participation. Travel and accommodation support for program events. Contribution to shaping future AI and economic policy discussions. Why This Residency Matters Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming economies worldwide. While AI offers tremendous opportunities for innovation and productivity, it also presents challenges related to wealth concentration, labor markets, financial stability, public accountability, and democratic governance. The Roosevelt Institute s Good Life Residents Program seeks individuals capable of proposing practical policy solutions that ensure AI serves broader public interests rather than reinforcing existing inequalities. Participants have the opportunity to contribute directly to one of today s most important public policy conversations while helping shape future economic policy. How to Apply Interested applicants should visit the Roosevelt Institute s official Good Life Residents Program webpage and complete the online application according to the published application instructions. Applicants should carefully review all eligibility requirements before submitting their materials. APPLY NOW Application Deadline Please read and complete this application by the end of the day on Wednesday, August 12, 2026, to be considered for the Good Life Residents Program on AI, presented by the Roosevelt Institute and Data Society. Reach out to rooseveltsociety@rooseveltinstitute.org with any questions or concerns. Program Term: 6 months (September–February 2027) Time Commitment: Part-Time (~5–8 hours/month) Location: Remote; Travel may be requested for select convenings Conclusion The Roosevelt Institute Good Life Residents Program 2026 offers an exceptional opportunity for experienced policy professionals and researchers to shape conversations around artificial intelligence, finance, and economic justice. Through expert mentorship, collaborative research, public engagement, and a funded six-month residency, participants can develop innovative policy ideas capable of influencing national discussions and future policymaking. For individuals passionate about AI governance, economic equity, and public policy, this residency provides a unique platform to contribute meaningful solutions while expanding professional networks and gaining national visibility.
